title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 1 of a draft 'Théorie de l'équivalence d'Albanese des cycles', which begins with 'Consulter Weil, Critères d'Équivalence'.

Definition 1.1 (previous page). Let X be smooth over k. A cycle z on X is Albanese-equivalent to 0 if there exist:
- a smooth connected T over k,
- a 0-cycle a on T of degree 0 with S_T(a)=0 in Alb(T)(k), where S_T is the Albanese summation map,
- a correspondence Z on X×T,
such that Z(a) = pr_{X*}(Z·pr_T^*a) is defined and equals z.

In modern terms, N^*(X) is the subgroup of CH^*(X) generated by images Z_*(a) of Albanese-kernel 0-cycles under correspondences from varieties T. In codimension p this is exactly H. Saito's F^2 of the Chow group (Nagoya 1979). It is the conjectural second step F^2 of the Bloch–Beilinson–Murre filtration.

This page states the structural properties (Prop. 1.2):
- (i), previous page: N^* is a subgroup containing the rationally trivial cycles. Take T=P^1 and a=[0]-[∞]. So N^* is determined by its image N'^* in A^*(X), the Chow ring, and Cyc^*/N^* ≅ A^*/N'^*.
- (ii) N'^* is an ideal of A^*(X). So A'^*(X) := A^*/N'^* is a ring. Proof idea: x·Z(a) = ((pr_X^*x)·Z)(a), by the projection formula.
- (iii) For a morphism f: X→Y of smooth quasi-projective varieties ('q.p.' replaces the struck 'variétés projectives'), f^* maps N'^*(Y) into N'^*(X). Hence it induces a ring map A'^*(Y)→A'^*(X): f^*(Z(a)) = ((f×1)^*Z)(a).
- (iv) For f proper, f_* maps N'^*(X) into N'^*(Y). It induces a group map A'^*(X)→A'^*(Y): f_*Z(a) = ((f×1)_*Z)(a).
- (v) Albanese equivalence implies algebraic equivalence, since a degree-0 0-cycle on a connected T is algebraically trivial. Hence one can speak of algebraically trivial classes in A'^*(X).

Together, (i)–(v) say Albanese equivalence is an adequate equivalence relation lying between rational and algebraic equivalence. It recovers:
- linear equivalence on divisors, since T→Pic^0(X) factors through Alb(T);
- the Albanese kernel on 0-cycles.

The proof starts with closure under sums, continued on the next page. Given parameter varieties T, T' for ζ, ζ', pass to T1 = T×T'. Pull back Z and Z' and use the 0-cycles a×{a'_0} and {a_0}×a'. Then Alb(T×T') = Alb T × Alb T', so the summation maps still vanish, and z+z' is realized. This needs a moving-lemma style choice of base points so that Z(a_0) is defined. A marginal note on the next page says 'Lemme à dégager'.
errors: Prop. 1.2(i), previous page, as transcribed, says N^* contains the numerically trivial cycles and that A^*(X) is classes modulo numerical equivalence. That would be false, since (v) gives N ⊂ algebraically trivial cycles, which is strictly smaller than numerically trivial (torsion in NS, Griffiths groups). Almost certainly 'num.' is a misreading or slip for 'rat.' (rational equivalence / Chow ring); the notation A^*(X) and the ring structure support this.

The sum argument (next page) silently needs Z(a_0), Z'(a'_0) to be defined for suitable base points and properness for pr_{1*}. Grothendieck flags this ('sous réserve que Z a pu être choisi tel que Z(a) soit défini'). With Fulton-style refined intersection it is a non-issue.

In (iii), passing to quasi-projective X requires the correspondence formalism with T possibly non-proper. The definition uses S_T, the Albanese of a possibly non-complete T. This is fine (generalized Albanese / or restrict to projective T) but not addressed.

ideas.what: Albanese equivalence of cycles of arbitrary codimension: z = Z_*(a) with a in the Albanese kernel of a parameter variety T
ideas.modern_name: Saito filtration F^2_S CH^p (second step of the conjectural Bloch–Beilinson–Murre filtration)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Saito (1979); also Bloch, Murre, Jannsen in the context of BB filtrations

ideas.what: Albanese equivalence is adequate: the trivial classes form an ideal, stable under f^* and proper f_*, yielding a quotient ring A'^*(X)
ideas.modern_name: adequate equivalence relation intermediate between rational and algebraic equivalence; quotient CH^*/F^2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Samuel's notion of adequate equivalence (1958); multiplicativity of F^2_S folklore/Saito

ideas.what: Alb-equivalence implies algebraic equivalence; so 'algebraically trivial modulo Albanese-trivial' classes make sense
ideas.modern_name: Gr^1 of the Saito/BB filtration, CH_alg/F^2, related to algebraic representatives (Murre)

missed.claim: A c.1965 Grothendieck draft defines the Saito-type F^2 filtration (Albanese equivalence in all codimensions) and checks it is an adequate equivalence giving a functorial ring A'^*(X), more than a decade before Saito (1979) and Bloch–Beilinson. This is a priority/historical point rather than new mathematics.
missed.quote: N'^*(X) est un idéal de A^*(X), donc Cyc^*(X)/N^*(X) ≃ A^*(X)/N'^*(X) est muni d'une structure d'anneau, noté A'^*(X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck, alongside the standard conjectures, considered an intermediate adequate equivalence tied to Albanese varieties. This is a precursor of the motivic filtration on Chow groups; of historical interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is routine (projection formula, functoriality of correspondences). What is notable is the early, unpublished formulation of Albanese equivalence for all codimensions as an adequate relation, anticipating Saito's filtration. Specialists would find it historically interesting but not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'Cyc^*(X)/N^*(X) ≃ A^*(X)/N'^*(X)' (the left side has N^*, not N'^*).

'Prouvons que si ξ, ξ' sont alb-équiv. à 0 sur X, il en est de même de ξ+ξ'' — the operation is a sum (the blot hides '+'), as the next page concludes 'N(X) est bien un sous-groupe'; the letters are ζ, ζ'.
The (v) parenthetical reads roughly '(Donc on peut parler d'éléments de A'^*(X) alg. équiv. à 0 !)' and continues into a partly struck line about 'alb-équiv. à 0 sur X'.
Struck proof line: 'Dém. (i) ζ est alb-équiv. à 0 ... Évident' — negation closure declared evident.
